text: capture_face_frames ( pg , layers ) Snapshot per-master face (ink) bounds: {layer_name: (left,bottom,right,top)}. Call this BEFORE deleting parts — it is the pre-deletion latch the region paste places against. Returns None if no layer had ink.
title: typerig.proxy.fl.objects.cjk.capture_face_frames

text: compute_gauges ( geo , S = 48 , y_weight = 1.05 ) Normalized gauge vector for one Geometry via the Qt raster + pure math.
title: typerig.proxy.fl.objects.cjk.compute_gauges

text: frame_for ( package , layer_name , advance , upm ) Em-square band in font units: x across the advance, y descender..ascender. Reads the active layer's master vertical metrics via FontMetrics(package, layer_name) - no setMaster, so the edit is undisturbed, and correct when the active layer differs from the active master. Falls back to the package's current master, then UPM-derived defaults. Returns (left, bottom, right, top).
title: typerig.proxy.fl.objects.cjk.frame_for

text: geometry_of ( pg , layer ) Build a Geometry from a given pGlyph + flLayer. Shared by the panel, the batch runners and commands.
title: typerig.proxy.fl.objects.cjk.geometry_of

text: get_geometry () Current glyph / active layer -> Geometry, or None when nothing to probe. Goes through TypeRig's pGlyph proxy: fl6.CurrentGlyph() returns an fgGlyph (fontgate) which has no getContours(); pGlyph builds the real flGlyph and the active flLayer. The extraction itself is in geometry_of() so batch runners and commands can reuse it on arbitrary glyphs/layers.
title: typerig.proxy.fl.objects.cjk.get_geometry

text: layer_ink_bounds ( pg , layer_name ) (left, bottom, right, top) of a layer's ink, or None if empty. Reads geometry via flLayer.getContours() (resolves shapes/components across masters); pGlyph.contours(name) can come back empty for non-active, component-built masters — which would make those masters miss the face.
title: typerig.proxy.fl.objects.cjk.layer_ink_bounds

text: measure_part_stems ( tr_glyph , pg , axis_layers , fallback_stems = None , tol_frac = 0.2 , snap = True ) Per-master (stx, sty) stems for a paste part, measured from its OWN contours. tr_glyph : typerig.core Glyph (the part being pasted). pg : the target pGlyph (for per-master ps_stems). axis_layers : master/layer names of the delta axis. fallback_stems : {layer: (stx, sty)} used when detection finds nothing (e.g. the global Virtual-Axis lib values). snap : when True, each master's measurement is snapped to that master's own PostScript hinting stems (so an off-grid value lands on a real stem); False = raw medians. Returns {layer: (stx, sty)} — only layers where a full pair could be formed.
title: typerig.proxy.fl.objects.cjk.measure_part_stems

text: measure_split ( pg , layer , idc , S = 64 ) Measured ⿰/⿱ split of one glyph/layer as a face fraction, or None. idc must be '⿰' or '⿱'. Thin wrapper: geometry -> raster -> boundary_ratio.
title: typerig.proxy.fl.objects.cjk.measure_split

text: part_stem_candidates ( tr_glyph , layers ) Diagnostics: {layer: (v_widths, h_widths)} raw stem-candidate widths that the detector found per master — inspect these when auto-stems looks off.
title: typerig.proxy.fl.objects.cjk.part_stem_candidates

text: rasterize ( path , frame , S ) Antialiased raster of a QPainterPath over the em-square frame. path : QtGui.QPainterPath in font units (WindingFill). frame : (x0, y0, x1, y1) font-space band mapped onto the S x S image. S : raster edge length (32..64). returns flat list[float] of length S*S, ink = 255 - gray, row-major with the TOP image row first — the identical contract as typerig.core.algo.cjk.rasterize_contours, so bands/zones stay portable between the two rasterizers. All-zeros for an empty path or degenerate frame.
title: typerig.proxy.fl.objects.cjk.rasterize

text: read_std_stems_by_layer ( pg , layers , lib_key = STD_STEMS_LIB_KEY ) Per-master standard hinting stems as {layer_name: [(value, 'V'|'H'), ...]}. Source order: 1. a font-lib mirror under lib_key ({master: {'H':[..],'V':[..]}}) — clean, no master switching; 2. else per-master flPackage.ps_stemsV / ps_stemsH read via setMaster (the same per-master access TypeRig's metric getters use), restored afterwards. Layers with no stems are omitted; returns {} if nothing is available.
title: typerig.proxy.fl.objects.cjk.read_std_stems_by_layer

text: region_bounds ( pg , layers , frac_for_layer , captured_faces = None , use_face = True , upm = None , default_face = None , margin = None ) Per-master target Bounds for an IDC-region paste — one entry per layer. frac_for_layer : callable(layer_name) -> (fx0,fy0,fx1,fy1) y-UP slot fraction, or None to skip the layer. Lets the caller apply a per-master measured split. captured_faces : {layer_name: (l,b,r,t)} pre-deletion snapshot; a layer that is absent (or whose face is degenerate) falls back per the chain below. default_face : a face rect used for masters lacking their own (e.g. the active layer's face — "a wrong face beats no face"). margin : imaginary-face inset (0..1 of the em) when nothing is measured. use_face : when False, always use the em band. Per master the reference frame is: own captured face -> default_face -> imaginary (em inset by margin) -> em band (cjk.reference_frame). NEVER a live face of the glyph under construction. Returns {layer_name: Bounds} (eNodesContainer bounds — the same type the node-selection paste path produces, so downstream fit/align/flip are untouched).
title: typerig.proxy.fl.objects.cjk.region_bounds

text: cornerRoundSquircle ( size = 100.0 , smoothing = 0.6 , isRadius = True , insert = True , radius = None ) Round an angular corner as a Figma-style squircle (superellipse) corner. Builds the corner from a central circular arc of radius R spanning an angle of turn*(1 - smoothing), flanked by two symmetric 'ease' cubic Beziers that blend the arc smoothly into the straight edges. The result is a 4 on-curve / 6 off-curve node structure (three cubic segments): ease-in, arc, ease-out. Arguments: size (float): Corner reach - the distance from the corner vertex to the point where the straight edge ends (font units), matching the meaning of the regular Round Corner radius. The circular-arc radius is derived from this and the smoothing. smoothing (float): Corner smoothing s in the range 0.0 - 1.0 (0.0 = plain circular fillet, 0.6 = iOS default). isRadius (bool): Interpret size as arc radius (True) or edge offset (False). insert (bool): Splice the new nodes into the parent contour. radius (float): Explicit circular-arc radius (None = derived from size and smoothing). Used to build one side of a stroked skeleton corner. Returns: list(flNode): the created node chain, or None if the corner was skipped.
title: typerig.proxy.fl.objects.node.eNode.cornerRoundSquircle

text: curveTo ( * points ) Draw a cubic bezier with an arbitrary number of control points. The last point specified is on-curve, all others are off-curve (control) points. If the number of control points is > 2, the segment is split into multiple bezier segments. This works like this: Let n be the number of control points (which is the number of arguments to this call minus 1). If n==2, a plain vanilla cubic bezier is drawn. If n==1, we fall back to a quadratic segment and if n==0 we draw a straight line. It gets interesting when n>2: n-1 PostScript-style cubic segments will be drawn as if it were one curve. See decomposeSuperBezierSegment(). The conversion algorithm used for n>2 is inspired by NURB splines, and is conceptually equivalent to the TrueType "implied points" principle. See also decomposeQuadraticSegment().
title: typerig.proxy.fl.pens.abstractPen.AbstractPen.curveTo

text: qCurveTo ( * points ) Draw a whole string of quadratic curve segments. The last point specified is on-curve, all others are off-curve points. This method implements TrueType-style curves, breaking up curves using 'implied points': between each two consequtive off-curve points, there is one implied point exactly in the middle between them. See also decomposeQuadraticSegment(). The last argument (normally the on-curve point) may be None. This is to support contours that have NO on-curve points (a rarely seen feature of TrueType outlines).

text: TypeRig Panel — UI configuration. Single source of truth for every visual / layout / sizing parameter in the GS3 plugin. There is exactly ONE place in the codebase where a pixel value, a font point size, a gap, a padding, or a default window dimension may be declared: this file, on the UI namespace.
title: typerig.proxy.gs3.gui.config

text: vanilla has no layout engine. Every widget is positioned by an absolute (x, y, w, h) tuple, so size / gap / padding constants leak into every panel module. Without discipline they drift: BTN = 28 in one file, BTN_W = 28 in another, an inline 4 somewhere else. Bumping a button by one pixel then becomes a six-file grep. Vanilla is a boilerplate nightmare compared to PyQt — the only way to keep it under control is to centralise every magic number. This module is that one place. Bump UI.BTN.SIZE here and every panel, the masthead, and the configurator move in lockstep.
title: WHY THIS FILE EXISTS

text: Fields are grouped under sub-namespaces by concern: UI.BTN — buttons (size, icon point size) UI.LAYOUT — universal spacing (gap, pad, margin, section title) UI.ENTRY — Panel entry fields, one preset per kind (STYLE / W / H) UI.SPN — numeric EditText dimensions (legacy: dialogs, IconAssist) UI.LBL — single-char label column, label-to-field gap UI.FORM — label + field grids, check boxes, text buttons UI.LIST — table (vanilla.List) dimensions UI.TINTLIST — colour-coded list: dots + row tint (gui/tint_list.py) UI.THUMB — outline thumbnails and the thumbnail grid (gui/thumbnail.py) UI.STATUS — status / warning text block UI.WIN — main window dimensions and minimums UI.MASTHEAD — masthead band geometry UI.ASSETS — asset filenames All field names are ALL CAPS to mark them as compile-time constants.
title: ORGANISATION

text: NO layout literal may appear in any gui/ , Panel/ , main_panel.py , or configurator.py file. Sizes, gaps, paddings, row heights, font sizes, window dimensions — all live here as fields on UI.<GROUP> . If you need a new metric, add a field here FIRST, then import it. Never inline a number "just for now". Pick the right sub-namespace or add a new one — do not flatten into the wrong group. New widgets register their tuning parameters here. A new slider widget adds UI.SLIDER.H , UI.SLIDER.TRACK , etc. The widget reads from UI internally; callers never pass raw pixel sizes through the widget's API. New panels follow the same pattern: alias the fields you use at the top of the file, then use the short names in body code: from gui.config import UI BTN = UI.BTN.SIZE GAP = UI.LAYOUT.GAP PAD = UI.LAYOUT.PAD TIT = UI.LAYOUT.TIT ... btn = IconButton((x, y, BTN, BTN), 'token', ...) The aliases are local readability sugar; the values still live in exactly one place. Do NOT redeclare BTN = 28 — that creates the second source of truth this file exists to prevent. Sub-namespaces keep things browsable. If a group grows past ~8 fields, split it. If a field doesn't clearly belong to one of the existing groups, add a new group rather than dumping it on the top level.
title: THE RULES (these are not suggestions)

text: bake_composite ( glyph , base_name , target_name , metrics = True ) Target layer of a composite glyph without the delta. The layer is made from the base input (components, anchors, width) when it is missing. With metrics: - metrics keys (glyph or layer): Glyphs computes them, syncMetrics(); - auto-aligned components: Glyphs aligns them to their base glyphs; - else width and component positions are scaled by the first component's base glyph: its target / base advance width (x) and outline height (y). The base layer is the reference, so a second bake does not compound. Returns {'created', 'aligned', 'scale': (rx, ry) | None, 'notes': [...]}.

text: vanilla.List2 colour coded by kind: dot column + row tint. Extra arguments (None = the UI.TINTLIST default): colors : {kind: NSColor name | NSColor | None}; LAYER_COLORS kind_key : item key / attribute holding the kind ('kind') tint : row tint alpha, 0 = off (TINT) filled : default dot state, True = filled (FILLED) fill_on_select : selected rows flip their dot (FILL_ON_SELECT) dots : False = no dot column (tint only) Everything else goes to vanilla.List2; alternatingRowColors defaults to False (zebra rows fight the tint). Columns are sortable unless their description says sortable=False; the dot column sorts by colour: the order of the kinds in colors (unknown kinds last). One column at a time: a new column sorts ascending, the same column again toggles; ties keep the item order. text: mount ( core_glyph , layer_names = None ) Push core Glyph metadata + geometry back into the FL host. Mounts each matching layer's shapes / anchors / guidelines via trLayer.mount, and copies glyph-level metadata (note, unicodes, mark). Glyph-level guidelines (UFO allows them on as well as on layers) have no direct FL equivalent — FL only stores guidelines per layer. They are pushed into every matching FL layer so no data is silently lost. A subsequent eject will return them as per-layer guides; this asymmetry is FL's data model, not ours. Args: core_glyph (Glyph) : pure core glyph to push layer_names (list or None) : restrict mount to these layers; None means all layers in core_glyph
